q: what kind of work do you do
a: TECHNYAH automates and repairs production equipment: robot cells, PLC and HMI programming, conveyor controls, machine vision, custom machines and production data. Most work is for manufacturers, packagers and distribution centers in Central Florida.

q: What does the name TECHNYAH mean?
where does the name come from
a: TECHNYAH comes from the Arabic word تقنية (taqniya), which means technology. It is pronounced tek-NEE-yah.

q: do you cover all of Florida
a: We are based in Lakeland, Florida. Polk County, Tampa Bay and Orlando are our home area, and projects elsewhere in Florida are scheduled by job.

q: Which industries do you work with?
what kind of companies do you work for
do you work with food plants
a: Food and beverage, packaging and consumer goods, logistics and distribution centers, metal fabrication and building products, medical device and pharmaceutical manufacturing, and agriculture, citrus and phosphate operations.

q: Can you help when a machine is down right now?
we have a fault on the machine
a: Yes. Send the fault message, the controller model and a photo of the panel. We reply within one business day and can often start with a remote look. I can take those details right now.

q: Do you work on equipment someone else built?
can you work on an old machine
a: Yes. Inherited machines with missing source code, drawings or passwords are a large share of troubleshooting and retrofit work. We document what is there before changing anything.
Troubleshooting and field service are billed hourly with a minimum call-out. Defined projects get a fixed price once we have seen the machine and agreed a written scope. Quotes are free.

q: How do I get a quote?
a: I can take the details here in about a minute, or you can use the full form, which also accepts drawings, specs and photos.

q: What should I send for a quote?
what do you need from us to quote
a: The controller and robot models, the fault message or the task you want automated, a few photos of the machine and panel, any drawings you have, and when you need it done. Missing items are fine; send what you have.
Every message is read by a person and answered within one business day. Each request gets a reference number so nothing is lost.

q: How long does a project take?
a: Troubleshooting is usually a matter of days. Controller and HMI upgrades run from one to six weeks. Robot cells and custom machines are set by hardware lead time, so every quote includes a dated plan with long-lead items listed.

q: Is there a minimum project size?
a: No job is too small when a machine is down. A single fault, one HMI screen or a one-day training session are all normal requests.

q: Who owns the program when you finish?
do we get the source code
do you hand over the PLC program
will we get backups and passwords
a: You do. When the job is paid we hand over the source files, backups, passwords and a short record of what was changed and tested.
Yes, where your network policy allows it. A remote session is often the fastest first step, and we can set up secure remote access as part of a project.

q: Which PLC and robot brands do you work with?
a: Robots: FANUC, ABB and Universal Robots. PLCs, HMIs and drives: Schneider Electric, Allen-Bradley and Siemens families. Send the model number and we will confirm before quoting.

q: Do you handle the electrical installation too?
a: We program, integrate and commission. Wiring and installation are done with licensed electrical contractors, and listed control panels are built by certified panel shops, all under one project schedule.

q: Do you provide stamped or sealed drawings?
can you sign and seal a design
a: No. TECHNYAH is an automation integrator, not an engineering firm. When a project needs sealed designs, they come from a licensed professional engineer brought into the project.

q: Do you work on water or wastewater systems?
a: No. We do not take municipal water or wastewater work. Our focus is manufacturing, material handling and industrial machinery.

q: How do you handle robot safety?
a: Every robot application gets a documented risk assessment before start-up, and guarding, scanners and safety logic are tested and recorded at handover. A collaborative robot is only fenceless when the whole application allows it.

q: Do you subcontract to other integrators?
can you work as a subcontractor
we are a contractor and need a programmer
a: Yes. We take defined programming, commissioning and troubleshooting packages for system integrators, machine builders and electrical contractors, under your contract and schedule.

a: Of course. Leave your name, email and a short message and a person will reply within one business day.

where do I send my resume
